result.summary: The intersection features standard pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks, signals, and sidewalks. However, high traffic volume and multiple travel lanes increase exposure for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Vehicle Exposure
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic, increasing the time spent in the conflict zone.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked and moving vehicles can obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade to continental or ladder markings to improve driver awareness of the crossing.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of an urban street with wide sidewalks and high-visibility zebra crosswalks adjacent to large-scale buildings. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and lack of a median refuge or visible signalized control at the crossing increase pedestrian exposure to traffic.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the roadway without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground at the zebra crosswalk

hazards.name: Lack of signalized control
hazards.description: No visible traffic signals or stop signs are present to regulate vehicle flow at this marked pedestrian crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection area in the center of the image

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide urban thoroughfare with a marked zebra crosswalk and signalized pedestrian controls. While basic infrastructure is present, the long crossing distance and the presence of tram tracks in the roadway create significant exposure and tripping hazards for pedestrians and cyclists.

hazards.name: Tram tracks in roadway
hazards.description: Embedded rails in the center of the crossing create a tripping hazard for pedestrians and a wheel-trap hazard for cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway within the crosswalk area

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic and a rail corridor without a physical refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Spanning the entire width of the roadway

hazards.name: Degraded pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and wear around the rail infrastructure can cause uneven footing.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface near the tram tracks

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane area to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Refresh the worn zebra markings with high-durability, high-visibility materials.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, traffic signals, and a marked crosswalk. However, the wide roadway width and significant pavement degradation in the intersection area increase risk for vulnerable road users.

hazards.name: Pavement degradation
hazards.description: Significant cracking and potholes in the foreground roadway surface can cause tripping or loss of control for cyclists.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic without a refuge island.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the degraded roadway surface to eliminate tripping hazards and improve safety for cyclists.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.
